You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 468a272ca49cc4e2f58f3c360643c3f6d313c146 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pierre-Louis Bossart <pierre-louis.bossart@linux.intel.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2021 17:22:25 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: max98373-sdw: add missing memory allocation check

We forgot to test that devm_kcalloc doesn't return NULL.

Fixes: 349dd23931d1 ('ASoC: max98373: don't access volatile registers in bias level off')
Signed-off-by: Pierre-Louis Bossart <pierre-louis.bossart@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Guennadi Liakhovetski <guennadi.liakhovetski@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Bard Liao <bard.liao@intel.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210607222239.582139-2-pierre-louis.bossart@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
---
 sound/soc/codecs/max98373-sdw.c | 2 ++
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+)

diff --git a/sound/soc/codecs/max98373-sdw.c b/sound/soc/codecs/max98373-sdw.c
index d8c47667a9ea..e178fdb6b899 100644
--- a/sound/soc/codecs/max98373-sdw.c
+++ b/sound/soc/codecs/max98373-sdw.c
@@ -786,6 +786,8 @@ static int max98373_init(struct sdw_slave *slave, struct regmap *regmap)
 	max98373->cache = devm_kcalloc(dev, max98373->cache_num,
 				       sizeof(*max98373->cache),
 				       GFP_KERNEL);
+	if (!max98373->cache)
+		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < max98373->cache_num; i++)
 		max98373->cache[i].reg = max98373_sdw_cache_reg[i];
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the lack of a check for the return value of the `devm_kcalloc` function, which is used to allocate memory for the `max98373->cache` array. If `devm_kcalloc` fails, it would return NULL, leading to dereferencing of a NULL pointer in the subsequent code when attempting to access `max98373->cache`, resulting in a potential crash or undefined behavior. The patch adds the necessary NULL check and returns an appropriate error code (-ENOMEM) if memory allocation fails.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>

    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the lack of a check for the return value of the `devm_kcalloc` function, which is used to allocate memory for the `max98373->cache` array. If `devm_kcalloc` fails, it would return NULL, leading to dereferencing of a NULL pointer in the subsequent code when attempting to access `max98373->cache`, resulting in a potential crash or undefined behavior. The patch adds the necessary NULL check and returns an appropriate error code (-ENOMEM) if memory allocation fails.
